blocks.text: Why freight broker business review is hard

The core of the problem is fragmentation. Your data lives in emails, carrier websites, and disconnected spreadsheets. When you sit down for a business review, you are not analyzing strategy. You are acting as a human bridge between systems.

Legacy TMS software often struggles on macOS. Many brokers rely on Windows virtualization tools like Parallels or Citrix. These add layers of latency and instability. If your reporting tool crashes when you generate a monthly load report, you lose momentum.
The hidden cost of manual reporting

When you report data manually, you introduce human error. A single typo in a pallet count or zip code ruins your margin analysis. Sales teams lose 43 percent of their time on quoting processes. This is time that should be spent on carrier relationships.
How to fix data reporting without new software

items: Audit your spreadsheet sources. Identify which reports are manual exports. Replace them with direct links to your TMS data.
Standardize your email templates. Use a consistent format for load tenders to make future automation easier.
Use keyboard shortcuts to speed up data entry. Learn ⌘ + F to find data and ⌘ + C or ⌘ + V for rapid transfers.
Clean your data. Delete duplicates in your sheets before running any review.
Create a dedicated folder in your browser bookmarks for all carrier portals.

blocks.text: The long-term fix is moving to browser-native TMS platforms. These run in Chrome or Safari without Java wrappers. They offer native analytics. This means your data is available in the core model rather than exported.
Always test software directly on your Mac. If a vendor mentions Java or Citrix, be cautious. These often fail on macOS updates.

faq.answer: Lazur works with any web-based TMS that runs in your browser. It sees your screen and helps you navigate or analyze data.
